memories.content: Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Clarify which stage of prototype fabrication or user study each requested resource is used for.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the personnel assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the equipment assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the time allocated to each procedure.
Verify that the planned number of formative evaluation iterations is feasible within the time for prototype modification and recruitment resources.
Include only the minimum functionality required to compare primary design assumptions in the scope of the formative evaluation prototype.
The user's iterative design plan can be judged feasible only if time and personnel are allocated for modifying the prototype between iterations.
Delays in participant recruitment can compress the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate review concerns: the reference focuses on formative-evaluation feasibility, resource allocation, prototype scope, and assumption labeling, while the compared frame focuses on defining and respecting the contextual boundaries of field-design knowledge. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other’s claims.

relations.reason: These memories split one reference-only disclosure policy across three assumption domains; the compared frame contains no claim about labeling assumptions.
relations.summary: Unverified assumptions about scheduling, recruitment, and technical matters should be explicitly identified as unverified.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-only guidance on explaining resource use, without a counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Requested resources should be mapped to the prototype-fabrication or user-study stage where they are needed.

relations.reason: These memories split one reference-only feasibility criterion across three resource dimensions; the compared frame does not address procedure resourcing.
relations.summary: Procedure feasibility is judged from its assigned personnel, equipment, and time.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim governs iteration-count feasibility and has no scope-aligned counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The planned number of formative-evaluation iterations should be checked against modification time and recruitment resources.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only prototype-scoping policy absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: A formative-evaluation prototype should include only the minimum functionality needed to compare primary design assumptions.

relations.reason: This reference-only feasibility condition concerns between-iteration modification resources, which the compared frame does not address.
relations.summary: An iterative design plan is feasible only when time and personnel are allocated for prototype modification between iterations.

relations.reason: This reference-only schedule-risk observation is independently useful and lacks a counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Participant-recruitment delays can reduce the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories express complementary parts of one boundary-setting claim: specifying population and environment and explaining their review significance.
relations.summary: The applicable population and usage environment should be stated because reviewers use them to judge the generalization boundary of results.

relations.reason: This is independent compared-only guidance for cross-site application and has no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Applying design guidelines at another field site requires specifying which workflow, technical-infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions must match.

relations.reason: This compared-only claim identifies contextual determinants of transferability; the reference frame instead addresses study feasibility and resources.
relations.summary: Transferability of field-design knowledge depends on workflow and technological-organizational infrastructure as well as user characteristics.

relations.reason: This compared-only observation identifies a specific overgeneralization tendency not asserted or contradicted by the reference frame.
relations.summary: The user tends to generalize results from one deployment site to all similar organizations.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame defines population, environment, workflow, infrastructure, and authority boundaries for generalizing field-design knowledge, and notes a tendency toward overgeneralization.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers transparent assumption labeling, procedure-level resource planning, iteration feasibility, minimum prototype functionality, and recruitment-related schedule risk.
